result.description: Free open-source WordPress ecommerce plugin; each merchant self-hosts a store exposing a REST API for products, orders, customers, etc.
result.auth_detail: Per-store consumer key/secret (generated in WP admin or via the /wc-auth/v1/authorize Application Authentication Endpoint) used as HTTP Basic over HTTPS, or OAuth 1.0a one-legged over HTTP. WP Application Passwords also work. No central OAuth2 provider; every store is its own server.
result.access_detail: No vendor app review, listing or partner status. Each merchant generates their own keys on their own store (or via the auth endpoint redirect flow). WooCommerce core is free open-source, so API access needs no paid plan; a dev can spin up a free local store. Caveat: the end user must run a store reachable over the internet (ideally HTTPS) with pretty permalinks. Hosting is the merchant's own cost, not a vendor plan gate.
result.api_notes: REST API wc/v3 covers products, variations, orders, refunds, customers, coupons, taxes, shipping, payment gateways, reports, settings, webhooks, system status etc. Also Store API (public/cart/checkout) and legacy v1/v2. Per-store base URL (https://store/wp-json/wc/v3).

evidence.quote: WooCommerce includes two ways to authenticate with the WP REST API.
The username when authenticating is your consumer key
Our core platform is free, flexible, and amplified by a global community.
Pre-generated keys can be used to authenticate use of the REST API endpoints.

This allows WC data to be created, read, updated, and deleted using requests in JSON format and using WordPress REST API Authentication methods and standard HTTP verbs which are understood by most HTTP clients.
The MCP implementation in WooCommerce is currently in developer preview.
WooCommerce does not bundle the MCP adapter.
You may access the API over either HTTP or HTTPS, but HTTPS is recommended where possible .
